meta.purpose: P7833 South Mississippi Project after the October 28, 2026 binding open season: length 215 mi, diameter 36, 42 in, renamed South Mississippi Gas Pipeline, route type Not mapped, notes rewritten, Richland Parish LA to George County MS, start March 2030, status ref added

verifications.note: A Pipeline & Gas Journal news story from late October 2026. It says Energy Transfer Interstate Holdings launched a binding open season for the South Mississippi Project on October 28, 2026, closing November 25. The pipeline would run about 215 miles from a proposed receipt point in Richland Parish, Louisiana, to a new delivery point in the George County, Mississippi, area. It would be either 42-inch or 36-inch pipe. The company has binding commitments from anchor shippers, plans to seek FERC approval, and expects service on or before March 1, 2030.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Status stays proposed. Energy Transfer opened a binding open season on October 28, 2026, and says it has binding commitments from anchor shippers. It has not yet decided to build and has not filed with FERC. The Pipeline & Gas Journal story is added beside the existing refs.

values.ResearcherNotes: Energy Transfer held a non-binding open season in late 2024 for a line of 100 to 150 miles from the Carthage, Texas, area, with 1 billion cubic feet per day of capacity that could grow past 2 billion. A binding open season ran from October 28 to November 25, 2026 for a redesigned line of about 215 miles from Richland Parish, Louisiana, to the George County, Mississippi, area. The pipe will be 36-inch or 42-inch, and service is expected on or before March 1, 2030. Anchor shippers have signed binding commitments. As of November 2026 there was no final investment decision and no FERC filing. The binding notice gives no capacity, so the capacity is still the 2024 figure. No route map found.
